items.text: The need to sleep interferes with. <break time="0.8s" /> Other more biologically pressing needs. <break time="0.8s" /> Such as finding and gathering food. <break time="0.8s" /> Building shelter. <break time="0.8s" /> And anything else you might do. <break time="0.8s" /> To ensure that your genetic line lives on. <break time="0.8s" /> Sleep is so important. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet so poorly understood. <break time="0.8s" /> That it led one biologist to say. <break time="0.8s" /> If sleep does not serve an absolutely vital function. <break time="0.8s" /> It is the greatest mistake evolution ever made. <break time="0.8s" /> That function is still a mystery. <break time="0.8s" /> It would be nice to say. <break time="0.8s" /> That sleep is nothing more than the time when a body rests. <break time="0.8s" /> But that would not be quite right either. <break time="0.8s" /> You can relax in a hammock on a beach all day long. <break time="0.8s" /> If you want to. <break time="0.8s" /> But after about twenty hours. <break time="0.8s" /> You will be in pretty bad shape. <break time="0.8s" /> If you do not fall asleep. <break time="0.8s" /> And stay that way for a while. <break time="0.8s" /> Humans need roughly one hour of sleep. <break time="0.8s" /> For every two hours they are awake. <break time="0.8s" /> And the body innately knows. <break time="0.8s" /> When this ratio becomes unbalanced. <break time="0.8s" /> Each hour of missed sleep one night. <break time="0.8s" /> Will result in deeper sleep the next. <break time="0.8s" /> Until the bodys sleep debt is wiped clean.
